title: Characterizing Post-Incident Software Evolution
abstract: arXiv:2610.27380v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: BACKGROUND: After a software incident, organizations attempt to improve the reliability of their software systems by conducting post-incident analysis and identifying actions to prevent or mitigate similar future incidents. Despite the importance of this activity, there is a limited understanding of the nature and characteristics of the software evolution triggered by the analysis process. AIMS: This study seeks to bridge this gap by providing the first empirical characterization of post-incident software evolution. We aim to establish an understanding of how these changes manifest, specifically focusing on how their characteristics (such as effort, location, and timing) differ from standard maintenance and evolutionary changes. translated_title: 事后软件演化的特征分析
translated_abstract: 背景：在软件事故发生后，组织试图通过事后分析和确定相关行动来防止或减轻未来类似事故的发生，从而提高其软件系统的可靠性。尽管这项活动非常重要，但对于由该分析过程所引发的软件演化的性质和特征，人们的理解仍然有限。目标：本研究旨在通过对事后软件演化进行首次实证特征刻画来填补这一空白。我们旨在建立对这类变化如何表现的理解，特别关注其特征（如工作量、位置和时机）与标准维护及演化变化有何差异。方法：我们对来自维基媒体（Wikimedia）的10年纵向数据集进行了混合方法分析，考察了1,302个任务和2,203个代码审查。我们从五个维度对这些变化进行了分类：目标、工作量、……
tldr: 本研究首次对软件事故后的演化进行了实证特征刻画，通过分析维基媒体10年间1,302个任务和2,203个代码审查的混合方法研究，揭示了事故引发的变化在工作量、位置和时机等方面与标准维护变化的差异。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first empirical characterization of post-incident software evolution, using a mixed-methods analysis of a 10-year Wikimedia dataset (1,302 tasks and 2,203 code reviews) to reveal how post-incident changes differ from standard maintenance in terms of effort, location, and timing.
